page.layout: One block of text with margin notes at the right. Running head at top, with the page number at top right. Reading order: running text from the top, then the verse heading, the verse with its margin notes, the Bezae paraphrase, the THESIS heading and the thesis text.

main_text.p: gitatem restringere. Postremò, non raró Deum ea propitium denegare: ne uideli- cet ijs abutamur, quæ dat iratus. Loquor de temporalium bonorum dispensatione & usu. Scitum est illud Augustini: Sæ- pe Deus multos non exaudit ad uoluntatem, ut exaudiat ad salutem. De summo Bono lib. 3.
main_text.head: VERSUS III.
main_text.p: Nam tu proiycere fecisti me in profun-dum, & in cor marium, & flumen circumLectio 17.17.Febr.1584[?] dedit me: omnes collisiones tuæ, & fluctus tui super me transierunt.
main_text.head: Paraphrasis Theodori Bezæ.

p.i: Nam tu me in profundum gurgitem, & ipsius maris intima, nautarum manibus proiciendum ipsa sortitione pronun- ciasti: ubi undiq; circumstantibus aquis, & fluctibus in se mutuo recurrentibus, obrutus iacebam.

main_text.head: THESIS.
main_text.p: Cum fides statuat, aduersa esse θεομα- χία: nequaquam proximis eorum causis irascitur.
Hæc θεὸς monet, æquissimum esse, ut

page.notes: The Greek word in the thesis, "θεομα-χία", is only partly legible on the scan and is marked for checking. The Greek word "θεὸς" in the last paragraph is also marked as read from a faint scan. The third margin note reads "158" with a flourish, so "1584" is doubtful. "gitatem" at the head of the page may begin with a larger letter that is not clear. The verse reference "lib. 3." is read from an ornamental numeral. A stray "m" sits at the lower left below the text, possibly a signature or stray mark, and is not transcribed. Printed "proiycere" and "marium" are left as printed.
